Early maturation in this species may be an adaptation to unpredictable juvenile survival in dynamic coastal environments, ensuring that some individuals reproduce even under suboptimal growing conditions. These size thresholds provide essential context for understanding the demographic structure of Etropus crossotus populations and for parameterizing stage-based models of population dynamics.
